hero_subtitle: Explore how Worcestershire County Council manages public money. Budget analysis powered by GOV.UK MHCLG data.
publisher_bio: This website was created by Tom Pickup, Reform UK county councillor for Padiham and Burnley West and Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care at Lancashire County Council. He is also parish councillor for Clowbridge with Dunnockshaw. Tom builds transparency tools that make public spending data easier to check.

Cabinet Member for Adult Social Care, Lancashire County Council
Parish Councillor for Clowbridge with Dunnockshaw
publisher_quote: It's your money. The more people understand where it goes, the better.

doge_context.political_control: Reform UK largest party (22/57) but in OPPOSITION since 14 May 2026; Green-led Conservative/Green/LD/independent alliance runs the council (Leader: Matt Jenkins, Green). NOC.

spend_triangulation.note: Transparency gross = £5.03B across every class in the published corpus. Procurement-paid (discretionary third-party payments) = £5.03B. Net revenue budget figures (where published) are smaller again because they net capital, grants received, and reserves movements — transparency totals include all of these.

procurement_paid.note: Discretionary third-party supplier payments — the real procurement footprint.

political_control.tenure_note: Reform UK lost the leadership of Worcestershire at the 14 May 2026 AGM after 12 months running a minority administration: a Conservative/Green/Liberal Democrat/independent power-sharing alliance took office with Green Cllr Matt Jenkins as Leader of the Council (his moderngov title: Leader and Cabinet Member for Local Government Reorganisation, Transformation and Government Lobbying). The removal followed Reform's internal leadership dispute in which former leader Jo Monk was suspended from the party in April 2026. Seat arithmetic (council member index, 6 Jul 2026): Reform 22/57 (largest), Conservative 12, Green 8, Lib Dem 7, Independent 6, Labour 1, Labour & Co-op 1; 29 needed for a majority.
